message:
docs(policy): drop three blanket prohibitions, fix two claims about deployment

Each of the three had taken a narrow fact and frozen it into a wide ban.

"No testing while RDP is connected, and results are not evidence either way" was
true of display refresh rate and DXGI and nothing else, yet it held up UI, logic and
network checks for hours at a time. Tests now carry a dependency tag and only the
ones whose requirement is unmet are skipped, with the reason. The inverse claim is
banned too: "UI tests are always environment-independent" is not a rule either.

"Always read host logs from the NAS, never the local copy, no exceptions" ignored
that failures before the uploader attaches, updater.log and the Windows event log are
not on the NAS at all. The NAS stays the default because it lets several machines be
compared against one source; local logs are allowed once device, time, version,
address and stream are pinned. Collecting logs in one place does not mean the clocks
agree, an absent log does not establish that something did not run, and one machine's
settings file does not diagnose another machine.

"Every response ends with a work summary" became a paragraph of recap after each
message. Intermediate reports are one to three lines; the detailed one belongs at the
end of a unit of work.

Two statements about deployment were wrong. A restart is not needed only for env
changes -- updating the server code or its modules needs one. And the manifest/sig
swap is not atomic as a pair: it is two renames, rename(2) is per-file, and
gnlink_deploy.sh says so itself at lines 435-436. The document was more optimistic
than the script it described.

Six clauses are new, the first of which exists because of the release that shipped a
notice with no button behind it: behaviour the user performs decides completion, and
a grep, a handler's existence, a displayed sentence or a PASS total is not evidence
of it. Also: test builds may differ from shipping builds while sharing the product
code, and what a non-admin build cannot prove is written down beside that permission;
work that needs no UAC is automated to the end and the user is asked once, at the end,
for the part only they can do.

CLAUDE.md is the detailed document now and AGENTS.md keeps the top-level rules. The
deletion limit, the workflow, scope control, the three roles, the push hold and the
private-key rule are unchanged.
